approval: Looks good. Go ahead and publish the 47 tickets as ready-for-agent. Make sure the unit testing and frontend quality requirements stay in each ticket.

tickets.title: Open a persisted event and sign in with scoped demo roles
tickets.deliver: Run the application locally, read one seeded event and game from PostgreSQL, and sign in as scoped administrator, organizer, scorekeeper, or read-only reviewer.
behavior: Bootstrap only the web/worker runtime, migrations, isolated demo seed and test harness needed by this slice; do not prebuild the entire schema.
The public scorecard and game detail show stored participants, current/latest draw, honest unknown scores, venue time and result state; reload/restart preserves data.
Seeded sessions enforce role/resource checks, and no public response exposes credentials, private person fields or internal payloads.
tickets.unit: Test current/latest/next draw selection, score-cell states and initial role/scope decisions using explicit expected outputs.
tickets.integration: Use real PostgreSQL for migrations, seed repeatability, session-scoped reads and denied writes; exercise the minimal worker/job runtime without mocking application persistence.
tickets.frontend: Establish the shared scores-first visual standard at phone, tablet and desktop widths: aligned/tabular scores, readable hierarchy, keyboard focus, loading/empty/error states and no placeholder controls.

tickets.title: Save live end scores from a mobile scorekeeper screen
tickets.deliver: An assigned scorekeeper starts a four-player game, saves or corrects an end, and sees the accepted change on the live homepage and game view.
behavior: Persist end scores and known hammer with actor/request attribution and an atomic audit record.
Retries are duplicate-safe; stale or out-of-scope writes cannot overwrite accepted state.
Show saved, unsent/uncertain and connection states honestly, preserving an unfinished edit through a temporary interruption without claiming full offline synchronization.
tickets.unit: Test four-player end validation, blank/unknown/unplayed distinctions, valid totals, version/idempotency decisions and save-state transitions.
tickets.integration: Submit valid, duplicate, conflicting and forbidden commands against real PostgreSQL; assert accepted scores and audit evidence commit together.
tickets.frontend: Browser-check thumb-friendly entry, clear game/end identity, labelled errors and visible public refresh without losing the selected draw or expanded card.

tickets.title: Confirm results and make ordinary auditable corrections
tickets.deliver: The assigned scorekeeper confirms a result, records a lineup difference or ordinary correction without admin approval, and fans see the correct final state and history.
behavior: Support normal/conceded/forfeit outcome distinctions under the implemented four-player profile; retain result versions and participant identities.
Default game lineup from the referenced event lineup; record differences without mandatory unchanged-lineup confirmation or claims that every declared player delivered stones.
Permit post-confirmation corrections with audit history and no second approver; preserve played-game evidence and flag downstream-started effects instead of building the deferred repair policy.
tickets.unit: Test outcome/confirmation/correction transitions, participant/winner validation and defaulted-versus-declared-difference lineup behavior.
tickets.integration: Confirm, retry and correct through authenticated APIs; assert original result versions remain recoverable and unrelated actors cannot alter them.
tickets.frontend: Make confirm/correct actions usable on a phone, distinguish provisional/final/corrected states by text and show useful correction feedback in scorer and public game views.

tickets.title: Submit and approve next year's event onto the calendar
tickets.deliver: An organizer submits a dated edition with divisions; a World Curling administrator reviews it and lists the approved event publicly.
behavior: Require organization, name, dates, city/country and proposed divisions while permitting initially incomplete venue/operational details.
Keep recurring series, dated editions, admission, registration opening and ranking eligibility distinct; creating next year does not overwrite last year.
Support ordinary organizer edits and administrator corrections with history, without a generalized amendment-reapproval engine.
tickets.unit: Test application validation, edition separation, allowed review transitions and independent admission/open/ranking states.
tickets.integration: Persist submit/review/edit actions and atomic audit records; denied actors and unapproved applications do not leak into admitted calendar reads.
tickets.frontend: Deliver clear organizer draft/submission and reviewer queue/detail screens plus a usable public event/calendar view, including field errors and empty states.

tickets.title: Delegate event approval and assign scoped event staff
tickets.deliver: World Curling grants scoped approval or event duties, and the correct reviewer or scorekeeper sees only the work assigned to them.
behavior: Apply geography/organizer/discipline/category scopes and named exceptions with one responsible approval authority and reviewer per application.
Record reassignment and World Curling override reasons; do not create contradictory independent approvals or implicit onward delegation.
Let authorized organizers assign their event's scoring access without granting global or ranking-publication authority.
tickets.unit: Test positive/negative scope matches, authority routing, explicit reassignment/override policy and role separation.
tickets.integration: Exercise administrative grants and actual guarded commands in PostgreSQL-backed sessions, including cross-event denial and revocation.
tickets.frontend: Show readable scoped grant/assignment forms and reviewer responsibility, with clear denied/empty views rather than global lists filtered only in the browser.

tickets.title: Manually enter teams and resolve core-composition identities
tickets.deliver: An organizer selects a team or assembles existing/new players into an entry; known core membership creates or reuses the right team and appears publicly.
behavior: Resolve identity from discipline and unordered core players, reuse returning compositions, and separate season registration from event lineup.
Five regular rotating players are all core; a designated alternate is not. Alternate/coach/name/position changes and temporary game rotation do not create another team.
Allow incomplete/provisional entries and new sport records without player accounts; preserve declared/defaulted participation and avoid a separate team approval gate.
tickets.unit: Cover order-independent matching, discipline differences, returning cores, five-core versus alternate classification, permanent core changes and temporary substitutes.
tickets.integration: Exercise automatic creation/reuse and duplicate requests with relational consistency; persist entry/lineup versions without overwriting seasonal rosters.
tickets.frontend: Provide usable team/player search and selection, add-player flow, clear core/alternate/substitute labels and a truthful public roster/entry summary.

tickets.title: Correct mistaken player selections and flag identity collisions
tickets.deliver: World Curling staff fix an ordinary player/entry identity mistake, while collisions remain visible issues instead of partial merges.
behavior: Suggest distinguishing existing records and permit a provisional person when uncertain; never merge by name alone.
Record factual corrections separately from genuine core transitions and retain their audit/source evidence.
Detect multi-record/team/entry/subject collisions, leave conflicting changes unapplied and retain a staff issue; defer cascading merge/consolidation tooling.
tickets.unit: Test candidate/ambiguity classification, ordinary correction rules and collision rejection without mutating partial state.
tickets.integration: Correct a mistaken selection through staff APIs and prove atomicity/history; attempt a collision and verify canonical and published evidence stays intact.
tickets.frontend: Make affected identity, proposed correction and unresolved issue clear; show successful correction or actionable conflict without a pretend merge-success screen.

tickets.title: Grant team-season representatives self-entry authority
tickets.deliver: World Curling grants a representative team-season authority and that person can submit or amend an entry for that team while organizers retain manual entry.
behavior: Support scoped submit/amend/withdraw/payment authority for the represented team-season.
A player-profile link grants no team powers, and authority does not transfer automatically to a different core-composition identity.
Use the existing canonical resolution and event-lineup behavior, with clear on-behalf-of actor attribution.
tickets.unit: Test team-season/action matching, profile-versus-team authority and denial after a core identity change or grant revocation.
tickets.integration: Exercise staff grants and permitted/forbidden self-entry commands with real sessions and database audit records.
tickets.frontend: Expose a representative's permitted teams/entries and staff grant controls; make team/season context and lack of authority explicit.

tickets.title: Open division entries with capacity and expiring holds
tickets.deliver: An organizer opens a configured division in open, reviewed or invitation-only mode, and entrants receive the correct acceptance/reservation state.
behavior: Require capacity, entry requirements, fee/payment terms and a documented format selection before opening; zero-fee fixtures can exercise the flow before online checkout exists.
Keep acceptance, roster readiness, payment and ranking eligibility separate; reviewed acceptance creates a defined payment window.
Expired holds release capacity, and competing accept/reserve operations cannot exceed capacity; exceptional late payment is only flagged, not automatically settled.
tickets.unit: Test mode/state transitions, prerequisite validation, reservation deadlines and capacity counting under a controlled clock.
tickets.integration: Use concurrent PostgreSQL transactions to prove holds/acceptance cannot overbook, plus expiry/retry and scoped action checks.
tickets.frontend: Give organizers and entrants clear open/reviewed/invited/held/expired states, remaining-capacity feedback and validation errors without a false paid/eligible badge.

tickets.title: Record entry charges, waivers and external payments
tickets.deliver: Staff and entrants see an accurate amount due with explicit discounts, waivers or externally received payments, independent of online provider processing.
behavior: Freeze charge currency and fee terms for an entry; later event fee edits do not rewrite prior charge history.
Apply normal fees to manual/invited entries unless an authorized reasoned adjustment exists.
Keep external receipts distinguishable from provider transactions and show payment status separately from withdrawal/readiness.
tickets.unit: Test minor-unit currency arithmetic, allowable adjustments, balance reconciliation and immutable charge-term behavior.
tickets.integration: Create and adjust charges through guarded commands, retaining an audit trail and rejecting unauthorized/invalid balance changes.
tickets.frontend: Render an understandable entry charge/history view with labelled fee exceptions and external references, avoiding a misleading online-payment success state.

tickets.title: Withdraw entries and invite replacements from the waitlist
tickets.deliver: Authorized staff or representatives withdraw an entry, release its place appropriately and explicitly invite a waitlisted replacement.
behavior: Maintain waitlist order/request state and record staff-selected invitations; do not automatically promote the next team.
Enforce representative/team-season or organizer scope and consistent reservation release.
Keep withdrawal and refund decisions distinct; preserve charge/payment history and avoid an automatic refund promise.
tickets.unit: Test withdrawal/invitation transitions, capacity release, deadline handling and separation from payment/refund state.
tickets.integration: Exercise repeated withdrawals/invitations and competing capacity claims against PostgreSQL without duplicate active entries or overbooking.
tickets.frontend: Give staff a usable waitlist/invitation action and entrants an accurate withdrawn/invited/held state with explicit payment/refund context.

tickets.title: Create accounts, approve player claims and edit profiles
tickets.deliver: A visitor registers, requests control of an existing player, receives World Curling approval and edits biography/handedness through the working site.
behavior: Provide configured account verification/recovery integration and safe local email fixtures; account creation alone links no player or team authority.
Let administrators approve/reject a claim and retain the decision; sport records remain independent of login accounts.
Limit player-controlled text fields to short biography and handedness and preserve other role boundaries.
tickets.unit: Test claim/link transitions, permitted field changes, validated profile input and denial before approval or for another player.
tickets.integration: Use real application sessions and PostgreSQL to prove ownership/link uniqueness and public projection boundaries; verify email/recovery adapters without exposing tokens.
tickets.frontend: Deliver complete register/sign-in/claim/status/profile forms and public profile reads with concise errors, keyboard access and no invented biography.

tickets.title: Review private photo submissions and publish approved images
tickets.deliver: A linked player uploads a replacement, sees review status, and an administrator publishes only the exact reviewed image.
behavior: Keep pending/rejected media private and leave the previous approved image visible until approval.
Validate and process uploads into durable storage; bind approval to immutable reviewed content rather than a replaceable upload key.
Retain approval/rejection actor, time and reason; do not expose upload credentials or private originals through public APIs.
tickets.unit: Test media type/size/input validation, request transitions, asset binding and public/private projection policy.
tickets.integration: Exercise upload, rejection and approval with controlled storage adapters and real PostgreSQL; prove a pending asset is inaccessible through public paths and cannot be swapped after review.
tickets.frontend: Provide usable upload/progress/preview/status controls and reviewer comparison, with clear rejection feedback and correct public image replacement at mobile and desktop sizes.

tickets.title: Stage a representative read-only Curling Crawler import
tickets.deliver: An administrator runs and inspects a staged import from a consistent export of the confirmed Curling Crawler project without changing its archive.
behavior: Translate source claims/records with fully parent-scoped keys, parser/export version and retained provenance; stream rather than inventing a live crawler dependency.
Preview final-score-only and complete-line-score games, incomplete rosters, known/unknown hammer and uncertain player/core identities.
Persist a frozen reviewable batch/digest and quality issues; staging alone does not publish or fabricate human certification.
tickets.unit: Use representative source fixtures to test scoped key normalization, translation, completeness/missingness and rejected malformed inputs.
tickets.integration: Read a representative real source export, persist/retry a staging job and query its preview/issues through admin APIs; verify source data is unchanged.
tickets.frontend: Show useful import progress/failure state, exact batch identity, previewed records and issue counts without presenting observation counts as unique games.

tickets.title: Approve historical batches and rerun imports safely
tickets.deliver: An administrator approves a reviewed batch and its historical events/results become publicly browseable with truthful origin and completeness.
behavior: Tie approval to the exact staged batch contents and map source identifiers to canonical events, entries, people/teams and games only where justified.
Rerunning an unchanged approved batch adds no duplicates; unknown core membership stays unresolved rather than creating invented team identities.
A reimport conflict with curated staff data retains evidence/issues and cannot overwrite the correction; defer complex field-level reconciliation.
tickets.unit: Test mapping/idempotency decisions, reviewed-digest checks and curated-conflict classification.
tickets.integration: Approve/retry/rerun against PostgreSQL and compare canonical identities/counts/history; verify unchanged import effects and no partial curated overwrite.
tickets.frontend: Show an explicit batch approve action and its result, public imported-source/completeness labels and inspectable unresolved issues with working event/game links.

tickets.title: Browse historical imported ranking editions
tickets.deliver: Readers and administrators select dated historical ranking observations without pretending they were recalculated by this platform.
behavior: Retain original labels/ranks/points, source/publication dates and optional subject mappings; unresolved historical rows remain viewable with honest status.
Keep imported observations distinct from calculated WCTRS run/approval records and preserve published-as-seen values.
Provide season/list/date selection and inspectable provenance, preserving meaningful point precision.
tickets.unit: Test edition selection, nullable subject mapping, origin/date presentation and meaningful decimal formatting.
tickets.integration: Load representative imported editions via approved batches, select them through public/admin reads and prove later mapping changes do not rewrite frozen observed values.
tickets.frontend: Build a readable dated ranking table/history selector with working resolved subject links and honest unresolved rows, plus accessible phone layouts.

tickets.title: Connect event, game, team and player discovery with favorites
tickets.deliver: Fans search the event archive and move between actual event/game/team/player pages while preserving useful context and browser favorites.
behavior: Complete the public pages around existing persisted data, with calendar/status/discipline filters and stable identity-based links.
Expose current results, next known game, core/alternate season context and known player information without lineage or fabricated participation.
Save favorites locally without account synchronization; preserve filters/draw selection/back navigation during refresh.
tickets.unit: Test search/filter/read-projection rules, stable context links, favorites serialization and current-versus-archived identity presentation.
tickets.integration: Query representative seeded and available imported records through public APIs, verifying privacy and correct identity/date/division scopes.
tickets.frontend: Browser-check homepage -> event -> game -> team/player navigation, search, empty/error states and favorites at phone/tablet/desktop widths with no dead controls or filler sections.

tickets.title: Schedule draw sessions and show known conflicts
tickets.deliver: An organizer assigns existing games to draw sessions/sheets, sees known clashes, and fans can browse the resulting schedule and draws.
behavior: Persist session/sheet/time revisions using explicit venue time zones and show current/latest/next draw consistently.
Detect overlapping sheets, entries and known player assignments across divisions; do not introduce a schedule optimizer.
Keep playing/status evidence distinct from a scheduled start having passed.
tickets.unit: Test overlap/availability decisions, session ordering, current/latest/next selection and timezone-aware schedule boundaries.
tickets.integration: Save/revise schedules through scoped commands; verify PostgreSQL relationships/history and public schedule projections agree.
tickets.frontend: Provide a usable organizer scheduling form/grid and public previous/next draw controls with explicit time labels, unclipped phone actions and clear conflict feedback.

tickets.title: Preview and run a single-knockout draw through public views
tickets.deliver: An organizer configures one documented single-knockout template, previews/publishes its persisted draw and sees confirmed results resolve future slots.
behavior: Introduce the shared relational graph/template-version contract with stable games, participants, explicit advancement and published revision history.
Use one bounded documented configuration, seeded entries and supported bye behavior; no unrestricted graph designer.
Expose usable bracket and game-list views; actual result/participant history cannot be rewritten by a later slot revision.
tickets.unit: Compare generated fixtures and advancement to an independently specified expected graph; check bye, slot/participant and progression invariants.
tickets.integration: Publish and advance via real score confirmation APIs, verifying stored graph/slot state and auditable revision behavior in PostgreSQL.
tickets.frontend: Deliver responsive preview/publish, linked bracket/list navigation and selected-team highlighting with unresolved-slot labels and keyboard-accessible game links.

tickets.title: Run the main 16-team triple-knockout demonstration
tickets.deliver: The main four-player demo operates a real 16-team triple-knockout draw with visible A/B/C routes, explicit qualifiers and next-game assignments.
behavior: Document one exact 16-team template, including its qualifier count/destinations, byes if any, and full A/B/C winner/loser routing before implementing it.
Use the stored graph, not loss count alone, and demonstrate representative A, B and C paths plus qualification/elimination.
Keep the current/next homepage draw, game links and bracket/list views consistent with confirmed results; defer played-downstream conflict repair.
tickets.unit: Use an independently reviewed expected routing fixture; cover each routing/qualification branch and whole-graph completeness without mirroring generator code.
tickets.integration: Drive representative and full bounded completion sequences through scoring APIs and assert final placements/qualifiers and next slots match the expected graph.
tickets.frontend: Verify a fan can follow one selected team on a phone and desktop through A/B/C and its next known game, with legible connectors and a readable list alternative.

tickets.title: Run one documented double-knockout configuration
tickets.deliver: An organizer selects and publishes one bounded double-knockout profile and fans follow its stored advancement paths.
behavior: Document the selected field size, routes, byes and qualification/final behavior; do not claim all variants are supported.
Reuse common scoring, schedule and published-graph interfaces without changing the main triple-knockout configuration.
Show honest planned/implemented/verified coverage for this named profile.
tickets.unit: Verify graph and winner/loser outcomes against independent fixtures, including elimination and any documented bye/final branch.
tickets.integration: Complete a representative profile using real persistence and score-confirmation APIs and assert resolved slots/history.
tickets.frontend: Make profile selection/preview and public bracket/list navigation as usable as the first template, with no generic template placeholder pages.

tickets.title: Run pooled round robin with basic public standings
tickets.deliver: An organizer publishes one documented round-robin/pool configuration and fans see its games and basic standings.
behavior: Generate a bounded documented pool configuration and persist its games/groups; expose wins/losses/ties as supported by results.
Keep unresolved standings ties explicit and leave playoff qualifier/seed selection manual.
Document the single-group/pool behavior exercised and avoid claiming every group/stage combination.
tickets.unit: Check fixture uniqueness/completeness and standings from independently listed game outcomes, including unknown/unfinished and tied cases.
tickets.integration: Confirm games and read updated pool/standings APIs with correct division/group boundaries and no duplicate game counting.
tickets.frontend: Provide readable pool tabs/standings/schedule links on phones, clear tie/pending labels and live refresh that preserves selected group.

tickets.title: Run a documented Page-playoff draw
tickets.deliver: An organizer supplies the manual seeds for one documented Page-playoff profile and its stored routes produce the expected final.
behavior: Persist explicit seeded games and advancement for the selected Page profile, with the same confirmation/history contract as other formats.
Keep source qualification a manual input instead of adding the excluded tiebreak engine.
Display named stages and unresolved opponents accurately.
tickets.unit: Compare all seed/winner/loser branches and final placement implications to a hand-specified expected fixture.
tickets.integration: Publish, score and complete the profile via the application and verify graph/slot/result consistency.
tickets.frontend: Make seed selection and public bracket/list views understandable and keyboard/touch accessible with correct event/game links.

tickets.title: Generate and score bounded Swiss/Schenkel pairings
tickets.deliver: An organizer runs one documented Swiss/Schenkel configuration, reviews each pairing round and scores the published games.
behavior: Specify field size, rounds and deterministic pairing/ordering rules for the supported profile; record seeds/tie inputs explicitly.
Persist pairings and inputs before publishing the next round; preserve organizer changes and prior rounds.
Do not add automated playoff-qualification tiebreaks or claim every Swiss/Schenkel variation.
tickets.unit: Verify initial/next-round pairings, deterministic equal-record ordering and documented rematch/bye constraints against independent fixtures.
tickets.integration: Generate successive rounds from confirmed results using real PostgreSQL and assert no duplicate/incorrect assignments or hidden overwrite of prior games.
tickets.frontend: Provide a usable review/publish-next-round flow and public round/standing navigation, with pending-result and validation states.

tickets.title: Select qualifiers and run a pooled-to-Page stage combination
tickets.deliver: An organizer manually resolves qualifiers/seeds from the supported pools into Page playoffs and makes ordinary auditable bracket edits.
behavior: Document one supported stage combination and explicitly record qualifier/seed decisions; tied qualification does not require automated policy.
Allow authorized organizer slot/path corrections without an administrator dispute case; retain draw and participant/result history.
If a correction affects already-started downstream games, preserve played records and flag the assignments for attention; defer comprehensive continuation/repair automation.
tickets.unit: Test compatible stage/qualifier mapping, allowed ordinary edits, invalid slot/entry rejection and started-game safeguard classification.
tickets.integration: Run pool results -> manual qualification -> playoffs and an ordinary correction through guarded commands, verifying preserved evidence and current public graph.
tickets.frontend: Make qualifier/seed selection and organizer edits clear, show updated fan brackets consistently, and expose affected-assignment warnings without a false automatic-repair claim.

tickets.title: Score mixed doubles and record required measurements
tickets.deliver: A mixed-doubles division can be entered and scored through the same working UI with its applicable scoring, participation and measurement profile.
behavior: Implement the documented men's/women's four-player and mixed-doubles profiles; do not add wheelchair/age-specific variants deferred by P-01.
Preserve discipline-appropriate hammer/end/outcome and LSD/DSC measurements where required, with unknown versus measured distinctions.
Keep core identity, registered roster and actual game participation separate, including temporary substitutions/recorded differences.
tickets.unit: Use sourced profile fixtures to test valid/invalid discipline-specific scores, outcomes, measurement units and lineup restrictions without imposing one universal four-player rule.
tickets.integration: Enter, score, confirm and ordinarily correct representative mixed-doubles games and required measurements against real PostgreSQL.
tickets.frontend: Verify a clear mixed-doubles entry/scoring screen and public line score, with applicable labels/measurement fields and no irrelevant four-player-only controls.

tickets.title: Finalize division results and preserve revised snapshots
tickets.deliver: An organizer finalizes a completed division, later accepts an ordinary correction and finalizes its revision without losing the original snapshot.
behavior: Record required outcomes, final placements, referenced entries/lineups/rules and exact frozen contents for each division independently.
Do not treat sporting finalization as ranking approval or an eligibility waiver; expose ranking-specific issues separately.
Allow the scorekeeper's correction without an admin gate, flag changed results and create a replacement finalization; defer transitive historical reassessment.
tickets.unit: Test finalization prerequisites, placement validation, revision/dirty-state transitions and snapshot-content stability.
tickets.integration: Finalize two divisions independently, correct and refinalize one, and prove old contents/digests remain unchanged with atomic audit evidence.
tickets.frontend: Deliver an understandable final-results review/finalize screen and changed-since-finalization notice with working revision/history access.

tickets.title: Collect an entry fee with sandbox Checkout and verified events
tickets.deliver: An authorized entrant pays a held entry through central sandbox Checkout and the application confirms the correct charge/place from verified provider state.
behavior: Use the existing charge/reservation model and scoped representative/organizer actions; a success redirect alone does not mark an entry paid.
Verify provider events, deduplicate deliveries and outbound requests, and retain request/provider/payment status and audit attribution.
Never overbook after released capacity; retain a late/exceptional outcome as a visible staff issue without implementing automated settlement policy.
tickets.unit: Test checkout/payment state classification, reservation/balance decisions, invalid/duplicate event handling and minor-unit amounts.
tickets.integration: Exercise signed provider fixtures, reordered/duplicate delivery and PostgreSQL capacity races, plus a real sandbox checkout when credentials are configured.
tickets.frontend: Show clear pay/return/pending/paid/failed/expired states and charge context on phone and desktop; uncertain outcomes never display a fabricated successful payment.

tickets.title: Issue and track full or partial sandbox refunds
tickets.deliver: Authorized staff request a full or partial sandbox refund and entrants/staff see its truthful transaction status and remaining balance.
behavior: Record refund actor/reason, idempotent provider request, pending/succeeded/failed status and amount/currency separately from withdrawal.
Reserve the refundable balance including pending requests so retries or overlapping requests cannot over-refund.
Demonstrate ordinary sequential refunds and flag uncertain outcomes; defer elaborate concurrent-operator reconciliation UI and automatic refund policy.
tickets.unit: Test refundable/pending balance arithmetic, valid partial amounts, repeated request handling and refund/withdrawal independence.
tickets.integration: Use PostgreSQL transactions and controlled provider responses to prove duplicate/overlapping requests cannot exceed the balance; perform normal full/partial sandbox checks.
tickets.frontend: Provide a clear staff amount/reason/confirmation form and readable refund history/status without promising success before provider confirmation.

tickets.title: Provision a scoped scoring feed and switch active sources
tickets.deliver: World Curling provisions a feed that scores/confirms/corrects its designated game, and authorized staff switch between that feed and manual scoring.
behavior: Issue/rotate/revoke event/action-scoped credentials with nonrecoverable secret verification and recorded client/request attribution.
Use the same score validation/version/idempotency rules as humans; only one active source controls a game.
Check current authority/source at the application point; reject stale-source work after a switch/revocation. Demonstrate sequential switching, not queue-draining/recovery automation.
tickets.unit: Test scope/action matching, credential/source decisions, duplicate/stale update classification and revoked-source rejection.
tickets.integration: Drive permitted/forbidden feed commands and human takeover against real PostgreSQL, including current authority checks and retained audit history.
tickets.frontend: Deliver usable client/scope/source administration and visible game source/takeover feedback; secrets appear only at issuance and never in public views.

tickets.title: Submit event, entry and finalization commands through partner APIs
tickets.deliver: An explicitly authorized partner can submit permitted event/entry data and finalize assigned divisions through the same domain behavior used by the UI.
behavior: Expose bounded command contracts and action/scope grants for event information, entries and organizer-level finalization.
Scoring access alone grants neither finalization nor event approval/ranking publication; preserve on-behalf-of client attribution and safe retries.
Return clear accepted/current/conflict/denied outcomes and documented API usage; do not invent another data-authority model.
tickets.unit: Test command/scope policy and input/response validation for allowed and denied partner actions.
tickets.integration: Compare equivalent human and partner command outcomes, audit attribution and duplicate behavior in PostgreSQL; deny unrelated scopes and publication attempts.
tickets.frontend: The existing admin/public views reflect partner changes accurately and expose client provenance where appropriate; no separate unimplemented integration dashboard is required.

tickets.title: Review official rosters, WCTRS sources and starting entitlements
tickets.deliver: World Curling staff inspect and maintain versioned seasonal registration, allocation and sourced starting-input records with visible ranking-readiness issues.
behavior: Separate platform core identity, registered ranking roster and point ownership, including five regular core members versus a designated alternate.
Record official rule/source editions, effective checkpoints and reviewed starting entitlements; missing required evidence remains unresolved instead of normalized away.

Document supported interpretations and independently worked input fixtures for the known counting-event/rounding ambiguities before verified calculations; an aggregate old total alone does not establish all future ownership inputs.
tickets.unit: Test roster/allocation membership and exact-share validation, effective interval/source requirements and blocker-versus-informational issue classification.
tickets.integration: Save/revise sourced records with staff authorization and PostgreSQL history, and prove unreviewed/incomplete inputs cannot be represented as complete approved evidence.
tickets.frontend: Provide a focused team-season/rules/input review with inspectable sources, version/effective dates and actionable issues, without a manual editable ranking-total shortcut.

tickets.title: Calculate four-player event assessments and point awards
tickets.deliver: An administrator calculates and reviews a four-player event's field strength and awards from a frozen result snapshot and sourced historical inputs.
behavior: Use the applicable 2026-27 rules, exact cutoff/pre-event ranking and event-edition inputs with eligible/excluded entries and explained factors.
Persist a replayable assessment/award revision and durable calculation job state; incomplete required inputs block a verified result instead of producing invented points.
Preserve source/rule/engine/input references and explicit adjustments; do not publish a world ranking list in this slice.
tickets.unit: Use independent sourced fixtures for field-strength/factors, award placement, eligibility/exclusion and stage-specific rounding, including missing/invalid inputs.
tickets.integration: Queue/retry calculations using real PostgreSQL, inspect completed/failed/blocked jobs and prove immutable input/result associations and duplicate safety.
tickets.frontend: Show an administrator useful assessment/award breakdown, inputs, exclusions and job/issues state rather than a bare unexplained points number.

tickets.title: Calculate four-player overall WCTRS draft lists
tickets.deliver: World Curling reviews complete men's/women's overall draft rankings with counted/excluded awards, ownership and dated carryover explanations.
behavior: Apply supported 2026-27 effective checkpoints, counting limits, weights, tie ordering, entitlements and ordinary adjustments without relying on lineage.
Keep core-identity reuse separate from restored point rights and retain frozen run manifests/contribution values.
Show unresolved required inputs/eligibility as calculation blockers; keep nonmaterial biography/unneeded-end-score warnings distinguishable.
tickets.unit: Work independent expected totals/orderings for normal and meaningful boundary cases, roster/ownership changes, carryover dates, caps/exclusions, exact arithmetic and required ranking ties.
tickets.integration: Calculate/retry/replay complete fixtures and reject incomplete ones through admin APIs using persisted awards/inputs; prove no duplicate or mutable contribution shortcuts.
tickets.frontend: Deliver a readable draft table and subject contribution drill-down with dates, meaningful precision, explanations and clear blocked/ready states.

tickets.title: Calculate Champion, Elite and Challenger series drafts
tickets.deliver: Administrators select and inspect the applicable men's/women's 2026-27 series drafts separately from overall rankings.
behavior: Implement the supported series-specific event classifications, schedules and counting/weight rules from sourced versions.
Reuse the recorded run/contribution/readiness contract while keeping different lists distinct and versioned.
Expose list/series selection and correct exclusions; do not invent series outside the accepted WCTRS scope.
tickets.unit: Use independently worked fixtures for each series' distinct checkpoints, classification, counted awards and ordering, not a copy of overall expected values.
tickets.integration: Persist/replay the different series lists and verify their inputs/contributions remain separate and compatible with generic publication readiness.
tickets.frontend: Provide useful series selectors, dates and breakdowns with no misleading overall/series mixing or placeholder list rows.

tickets.title: Calculate mixed-doubles field strength and event awards
tickets.deliver: Administrators assess a mixed-doubles event using its pair/player and required four-player ranking inputs and inspect its award breakdown.
behavior: Use sourced 2026-27 mixed-doubles formulas and the exact required historical inputs; pair-only history cannot silently substitute for missing individual/team inputs.
Retain eligibility, effective roster/participation evidence, cutoff and factor explanations with frozen result snapshots.
Blocked required inputs remain visible; document the known counting-rule interpretation instead of treating inconsistent prose as resolved fact.
tickets.unit: Verify independently worked strength/award examples, individual/team contribution branches, cutoffs, exclusions and rounding with valid and incomplete input sets.
tickets.integration: Calculate/retry from persisted mixed-doubles results and four-player inputs, retaining all source/subject relationships and issue states.
tickets.frontend: Show the mixed-doubles assessment as an understandable breakdown with player/pair links, source dates and specific readiness issues.

tickets.title: Calculate mixed-doubles pair and individual draft lists
tickets.deliver: World Curling reviews the supported mixed-doubles pair, female-player and male-player draft rankings with independent contributions and history.
behavior: Apply each supported subject/list's 2026-27 counting, ownership, weighting and tie-ordering rules to sufficient sourced inputs.
Keep person subjects separate from pair identities and preserve counts/exclusions/effective dates in replayable runs.
Do not auto-publish, fabricate inputs or add Member Association/other discipline lists.
tickets.unit: Use independently worked pair and individual expected totals/orderings across relevant dated checkpoints, partner changes, excluded events and rounding branches.
tickets.integration: Persist and replay all three subject/list types and verify correct subject mappings, contributions and incomplete-input blocking.
tickets.frontend: Make pair/individual selection and contributor drill-down readable at mobile and desktop widths, with clear list names and no mislabeled team-only views.

tickets.title: Approve and publish complete dated WCTRS lists
tickets.deliver: A World Curling administrator compares and approves a complete dated list, and public rankings expose that exact approved publication.
behavior: Use a list/subject-type-independent review/publication contract compatible with overall, series and mixed-doubles draft producers.
Block publication on required calculation/eligibility issues; allow only informational acknowledgements unrelated to the calculation, without an exception/waiver engine.
Freeze inputs, contributions, outputs and decision evidence; expose effective and publication dates separately and exclude drafts/live projections from public defaults.
tickets.unit: Test readiness gating, informational-versus-blocking issues, authorized publication transitions, comparison rules and meaningful precision.
tickets.integration: Attempt incomplete/forbidden approval and publish/replay a complete list in PostgreSQL; prove outputs cannot be silently overwritten and published reads are exact.
tickets.frontend: Deliver a focused comparison/approve flow and polished public list/filter/contribution views with actual data and honest blocked/imported/draft/published labels.

tickets.title: Audit ranking history and approve a direct replacement
tickets.deliver: An ordinary result correction leads to revised finalization, a directly affected draft and an approved replacement, while administrators can audit both publications.
behavior: Preserve the original finalized snapshot/publication and show what changed, who acted and the exact calculation inputs/engine revision.
Support replay and published-as-seen versus corrected-effective-date views with a direct replacement chain.
Do not build transitive later-event field-strength reassessment; retain original later assessment inputs and flag broader impacts as unresolved instead of claiming full cascade completion.
tickets.unit: Test immutable-content/digest comparison, direct supersession/date selection and changed-input classification with independent expected results.
tickets.integration: Complete correction -> revised finalization -> recalculation -> approval through real commands and assert original snapshots/runs remain unchanged and auditable.
tickets.frontend: Provide useful history/version comparison, actor/reason and contribution navigation, with a clear limitation for wider unprocessed impacts and no fake recalculated status.

tickets.title: Show team win-loss records and title counts
tickets.deliver: Fans inspect the first minimum analytics view: supported team win/loss records and titles with explicit sample and result coverage.
behavior: Document counting rules for confirmed/unknown/tied/forfeit/void results and titles from finalized placements; count a logical game/division once across revisions.
Filter by the supported discipline/date/event context and retain source/completeness information.
Do not infer that every listed/defaulted player played or expand into deferred streak/rivalry statistics; any player-level attribution must state its evidence.
tickets.unit: Use small hand-counted fixtures for records, title counts, revisions, missing outcomes and scope filters with independently expected denominators.
tickets.integration: Query persisted results/finalizations and ordinary corrections through analytics APIs, proving no double counting or private-data leakage.
tickets.frontend: Render purposeful records/title tables or charts with filters, units/sample labels, working team/event links and honest no-data states at all target widths.

tickets.title: Chart approved rank and points history with contributions
tickets.deliver: Fans compare approved ranking/points history and inspect contributing events across calculated publications and honestly labelled imported history.
behavior: Use dated approved/observed values, preserving effective-versus-publication-time and imported-versus-calculated origin.
Expose contribution detail where it exists and explicitly mark unavailable historical explanation rather than reconstructing it silently.
Keep core-composition subjects distinct and person histories stable without deferred team lineage.
tickets.unit: Test history/date selection, series alignment, contribution reconciliation, sparse-history handling and meaningful decimal values against explicit fixtures.
tickets.integration: Read representative calculated and imported publications through public APIs and verify graph/table values agree with frozen rows and selected context.
tickets.frontend: Provide readable chart plus table access, date/list filters, comparison/point drill-down and keyboard/mobile usability without decorative or invented trend lines.

tickets.title: Show blank and steal rates from known end data
tickets.deliver: Fans use the minimum scoring-pattern view to inspect blank and steal rates computed from suitable observed ends.
behavior: Define/document numerators, denominators and team/population scope before implementation, using actual completed ends and known hammer where required.
Exclude unknown-required fields and unplayed/post-concession ends; distinguish zero sample from a true zero rate and avoid revision double counting.
Limit the offered measures to P-05 blank/steal rates and supported disciplines with clear filters and coverage.
tickets.unit: Verify hand-counted numerator/denominator examples, hammer perspectives, missing/unplayed data, corrections and zero-sample behavior.
tickets.integration: Calculate rates from stored games/ends and confirm filtered API values, sample counts and displayed corrections agree.
tickets.frontend: Show the two useful rates with sample/coverage, clear definitions and filter state, readable on a phone without unexplained percentages.

tickets.title: Show observed win rates by end, margin and hammer
tickets.deliver: Fans inspect the minimum situational analytics view using actual comparable game states and known final outcomes.
behavior: Document the state timing, win/sample definition and population filters, separating supported disciplines and relevant regulation/rule contexts.
Use only observed situations with the required margin/hammer/outcome evidence; exclude hypothetical ends after concession and unknown required data.
Show sample sizes and unknown/zero-sample states; do not present calibrated live prediction or expand the metric inventory.
tickets.unit: Compare matrix cells/filters to independent hand-worked game-state fixtures, including both hammer perspectives, missing outcomes and conceded games.
tickets.integration: Read persisted score/outcome history and verify API cells, population filters and sample counts against the same immutable fixture evidence.
tickets.frontend: Provide an understandable filtered table/heatmap with accessible cell details and mobile table access, showing exact context and samples rather than unsupported certainty.

tickets.title: Aggregate approved curling news into working source links
tickets.deliver: Staff configure approved external feeds and fans browse concise news cards that open the original publisher.
behavior: Fetch only approved source feeds, record publisher/date/supplied excerpt/original URL and deduplicate items.
Allow staff to manage sources and hide unsuitable/duplicate items; record failures and stale fetch state without inventing news.
Keep untrusted text/URLs safely rendered and exclude editorial authoring/full-article republication.
tickets.unit: Test feed normalization, identity/deduplication, date/URL validation, safe text projection and hide/source-status filtering.
tickets.integration: Run retryable fetch jobs with controlled feed fixtures and PostgreSQL, proving duplicate-safe persistence and public/staff permission boundaries.
tickets.frontend: Create useful news cards and source-management controls with honest empty/failure states and working external links, without generated filler or inactive buttons.

tickets.deliver: The implemented application runs as web/worker/PostgreSQL services with a reviewer-accessible HTTPS domain and configured provider adapters.
behavior: Use actual repository/provider/domain inputs when supplied; this ticket may deploy an early completed slice and accept later feature migrations without waiting for all product branches.

Document setup, health/jobs, migration/release and operator/API use; do not activate live payments or add the excluded independent backup/recovery project.

tickets.integration: Perform hosted web/worker/database persistence, authentication, configured provider and restart/job smoke checks, with real credentials kept out of logs/recordings.
tickets.frontend: Verify the live HTTPS page/sign-in and currently delivered flows on phone/desktop; clearly label demo data and report any unresolved deployment inputs instead of claiming a successful host.
